intent: Add caching so repeated weather requests do not hit the upstream forecast provider
summary: Put a short-lived in-memory cache in front of the forecast provider. The endpoint checks the cache first, calls upstream only on a miss, stores the result, and shapes hits and misses through the same response schema.

concepts.title: Weather endpoint
concepts.purpose: Receives GET /api/weather/:city, validates the city, and coordinates the lookup.
outputs: JSON weather response or an error status

concepts.title: Cache lookup
concepts.purpose: Normalizes the city into a cache key and returns a stored forecast if it has not expired.

invariants.claim: Cities that differ only by letter case or surrounding spaces share one cache entry.

concepts.title: Upstream forecast call
concepts.purpose: Fetches a fresh forecast from the slow, metered provider. Only reached on a cache miss after this feature.

concepts.title: Cache write with TTL
concepts.purpose: Stores a fresh forecast with the time it was fetched, expiring after 60 seconds.

concepts.title: Response shaping
concepts.purpose: Builds the JSON body through the WeatherResponse schema for both hits and misses.

invariants.claim: Cached and uncached responses have the same schema.

steps.title: Create a TTL cache module
steps.expectedBehavior: A reusable in-memory cache exists with get, set, expiry, and a case-insensitive key helper. No endpoint behavior changes yet.

steps.title: Check the cache before calling upstream
steps.expectedBehavior: Repeated requests for the same city within 60 seconds reach the provider once; responses are unchanged in shape.

steps.title: Prove hits and misses share one schema
steps.expectedBehavior: Tests show cached and uncached responses both match WeatherResponse and expire after the TTL.

assumptions: One server process, so an in-memory cache is enough; no shared cache across instances.
A 60-second TTL is acceptable staleness for weather data.
